verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I couldn't talk to you as Spirit-led people, but as people shaped by human nature—as infants in Christ.
I fed you milk, not solid food, because you weren't ready for it. And you're still not ready,
because you're still living by human nature. As long as jealousy, arguments, and divisions are among you, aren't you living by human nature and acting like everyone else?
When one of you says, ‘I follow Paul,’ and another, ‘I follow Apollos,’ aren't you acting like everyone else?
So who is Apollos? Who is Paul? We're servants through whom you came to believe, each doing what the Lord assigned.
I planted the seed, Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.
So the one who plants and the one who waters aren't the main thing. God, who makes it grow, is.
The one who plants and the one who waters share the same purpose, and each will be rewarded according to their own work.
We are God's co-workers. You are God's field, God's building.
By God's grace to me, I laid a foundation like a skilled builder, and someone else is building on it. Each person must be careful how they build.
No one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid: Jesus Christ.
Some may build on this foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw.
Each person's work will become clear. The Day will reveal it, because it will be uncovered by fire; the fire will test the quality of each person's work.
If what someone built on the foundation survives, they'll receive a reward.
If their work burns up, they'll suffer loss. They themselves will be saved, but only as someone escaping through fire.
Don't you know that you are God's temple and God's Spirit lives in you?
If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy them. God's temple is holy, and you are that temple.
Don't fool yourselves. If any of you thinks you're wise by this world's standards, you should become a fool in this world's eyes so you can become truly wise.
The wisdom of this world is foolishness to God. Scripture says, ‘He catches the wise in their own cleverness.’
And again, ‘The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are pointless.’
So don't brag about people. Everything belongs to you:
whether Paul, Apollos, or Cephas; the world, life or death; the present or the future. Everything belongs to you,
you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
